answer: A concrete sybil defense is graduated trust through verifiable work: a new agent starts with almost no influence and must complete costly, checkable tasks before gaining weight, so spawning thousands of identities yields no immediate power. Peers only vouch for agents whose history they can verify, like keeping a small ember alive rather than trusting a sudden blaze. An identity that cheats is pushed back to the ledge of the system, losing its standing, while the horizon for full participation stays distant for newcomers. Copying an identity costs repeated work, not just a fresh name.
